A CPU pin here is only a measurement on a box that is not oversubscribed, and the lane says so now instead of reporting contention as a regression. measurement_conditions below records what these pins were taken under -- loadavg 9 to 30 on a 32-core box, 0.28 to 0.94 runnable processes per core -- and what happens above it: at loadavg 30 a task-clock triple spread 38% to 64% while instructions:u over the same runs spread 0.00002% to 0.129%. The ceiling is normalised by core count on purpose: a raw loadavg of 30 is a third of a 32-core desk and fifteen times a 2-core runner. measurement_conditions: Measured 2026-08-28 on a 32-core box SHARED with other agents' gates, loadavg 9 to 30 throughout. THE CPU PINS ARE THEREFORE LOADED-BOX FIGURES AND ALL SIX WANT RE-CONFIRMING ON A QUIET BOX, boot first (95% band, 78% excursion, and the shortest region at 0.13s), then term-in (80%/63%), cursor-step and term-out (75%/61-62%), then space-pair (45%/34%) and error-ball (40%/32%). HOW THE PINS WERE TAKEN: min-of-FIFTEEN for the pin, min-of-three for each comparison. The minimum converges on the uncontended value, and fifteen samples land within 5% of the lowest reading ever seen for every case where three samples do not; re-pin with `sh bench.sh --update --rounds 15`. release_0_8_0_boot_environment_note:
NOT RE-PINNED 2026-09-06, and this says why, because the row read two numbers on one source during this pass and the second one is the measurement environment rather than the engine. In a FRESHLY CLONED tree, built and warmed and left alone, boot reads 382,606 and 382,607, which is the pin above and inside its four-inference allowance. In a tree whose files have been REWRITTEN IN PLACE -- a `cp` of the same bytes over 236 tracked files, or a `git checkout -f` per commit through a sweep -- it reads 382,625, 382,627 three times, 382,628 and 382,629, twenty-one higher, and the sweep's own points at 82c1ab65 and 5bdf3d60 both read 382,629 for the same reason. Every reading is deterministic within its tree: three identical samples, every time.

What it is NOT. Reverting the four engine files whose comments the provenance pass rewrote, with the .qlf set cleared and rebuilt before each arm and three runs per arm, reads 382,627 in all nine runs, so no source difference explains it. libcmetta.so and benchmarks/cases are byte-identical across rebuilds (md5 350ec656 and a7e45f99 before and after). Clearing and regenerating the .qlf set inside one tree does not move it, and neither does removing the package cache under repos/. What is left is the file state a rewrite leaves behind, and the mechanism inside that is not established [assumed: why rewriting a tracked file with its own bytes costs this row twenty-one inferences is unexplained; the controls above rule out the sources, the artifacts, the .qlf regeneration and the package cache].

The same hunt found the neighbouring hazard, on term-in's retired-instruction row. The .qlf set is not one image: a set built from scratch by qlf_boot.pl and a set in which a few units were recompiled into an otherwise-fresh one give 4,398,146,45x and 4,385,666,00x, 0.28% apart against a 0.15% band, each stable across repeated runs and across the whole engine suite running in front of it. Clearing the set and letting qlf_boot.pl rebuild it -- the tree's own rule after any checkout -- returns the first, which the pin above already covers. So both of this seat's fragile rows have the same remedy, and it is the one this repository already writes down: clear the .qlf and boot once, in a tree you have not written over.
